column1: # tab-separated: NAME ROUTE CWD STDIN ENV PROGRAM ARG...
# CWD is under /home/operator/cports/ on ABSD (writable; the program is started with
# it as its working directory, because sessions start in read-only / and temporary
# names are relative to the working directory, SPEC A12) and a temporary directory
# with the same contents on Linux. STDIN is - or a file of CWD. ENV must be - on the
# shell route: the session environment is empty and absd-sh cannot set variables
# (C-INTERFACE.md 6); the Linux side runs with an empty environment plus TZ=UTC.
# "# outputs NAME: path..." lines name files compared byte for byte after the case;
# "# expect NAME: ..." lines state the observation a scenario must show;
# "# retained NAME: path..." and "# removed NAME: path..." name files the case keeps
# or deletes on purpose (exempt from the resource census, removed ones checked gone);
# "# timeout NAME: seconds" overrides the 600 s default.
# ROUTE is shell (one SSH exec session, compared with Linux), probe (run on ABSD only,
# recorded, never compared: it supplies the Linux runner's inputs) or scenario (a
# multi-session or cut scenario the harness drives by name, CPORTS-HARNESS.md 5.4;
# PROGRAM names the scenario and ARG... its parameters).
# posix.*: the adapter's guest probe (c/posix/tests/guest/posixprobe.c). `agree` must equal
# Linux; the others are listed divergences pinned in cports/absd-expected/.

# expect sqlite.home: ABSD prints "-- warning: cannot find home directory; cannot read ~/.sqliterc" on stderr and then 1, status 0 (getpwuid NULL: no user database, SPEC A8; no HOME: SPEC A20); Linux prints 1 (its passwd database names a home). The Linux twin (the reference, not the guest; A20 is about the guest) runs with HOME set to an empty directory under the work directory, and the harness checks that the running user's passwd home holds no ~/.sqliterc or ~/.config/sqlite3/sqliterc (the Linux shell asks getpwuid before HOME). Listed divergence (CPA-013, CPA-037)

# expect sqlite.temp-nomem: (SPEC A18) ABSD: the sort past the 32 MiB heap window is SQLITE_NOMEM ("Error near line 10 of temp-nomem.sql: out of memory") and the shell continues: "still running|1"; Linux (the same SQLITE_TEMP_STORE=3, an unbounded heap) prints 40000, "still running|1" and "ok", status 0. Then a fresh session's "PRAGMA integrity_check; SELECT count(*) FROM t;" prints ok and 1 on both sides (the database intact). Pinned as a DEFECT (R16) until candidate 2; since R16 the in-process PRAGMA integrity_check after the NOMEM prints ok, and the case is a NATIVE LIMIT divergence (divergences.txt; CPA-049, CPA-060) pinned byte for byte. A process death (status 128 or 134, nothing after) would be a DEFECT of A18 itself

# expect sqlite.excl-busy: (SPEC A7 step 1, A17 lifetime) holder A in an open session sends "BEGIN; INSERT INTO t VALUES(3,'three');" then ".print HELD"; after HELD arrives on A's SSH stream, B's "sqlite3 -batch -vfs unix-excl x.db 'SELECT count(*) FROM t;'" prints "Parse error in 5th command line argument: database is locked (5)" on stderr, exits 1, and returns in under 5 s (the native lock never waits); after A's COMMIT B is still denied (unix-excl keeps the lock for the connection's life); after A's .quit and normal session end B prints 3 and exits 0. The Linux twin (host processes) prints the same

# expect sqlite.excl-release: (SPEC A7 step 2) A holds "BEGIN; INSERT INTO t VALUES(4,'four');", B is denied; A's session is killed while it holds the lock; the file server releases A's channel (drop_opens, fsd/src/server.rs:437-449) and with it the native lock; B's same query then prints "3" and exits 0 (A's uncommitted row absent); the directory's file list is compared with Linux's after the same steps (on the reference an x.db-journal without a synced header remains: it is not hot, so B neither rolls it back nor deletes it); a difference is a CPORTS SCENARIO NOTE

# expect sqlite.excl-concurrency-loss: (SPEC A10; SQLITE-VFS.md 10) Linux with -vfs unix: holder A in "BEGIN; INSERT INTO t VALUES(9,'nine');", reader B prints 3 and exits 0; Linux with -vfs unix-excl and ABSD with -vfs unix-excl: B prints "Parse error in 5th command line argument: database is locked (5)" and exits 1; then A quits on each side (rollback by exit) and the count stays 3. Passes when ABSD equals Linux unix-excl and Linux unix shows the reader succeeding; the difference is the declared loss

# expect sqlite.excl-crash: (SPEC A7 step 3) A runs "PRAGMA cache_size=10; BEGIN;" and 2,000 inserts, prints SPILLED; QEMU is stopped on SPILLED and the image copied; next boot B runs "PRAGMA integrity_check; SELECT count(*) FROM t;" and prints "ok" then 3; x.db-journal absent afterwards; the host's sqlite3 module on x.db plus x.db-journal from the copy, and on x.db after B, prints the same. The Linux twin kills A with SIGKILL instead and prints the same. Evidence is this guest scenario only; the host mock's lock (R8) is never evidence
